# What AI Models on Cloud Platforms Can Do Now, in Plain Language

> **In short:** Together AI says Tencent's flagship model, Hy4, now runs on its platform and can read images as well as text. Picsart says its Media Studio works inside Claude, turning your clips into finished videos in the same chat. Both show AI doing practical jobs, not only answering questions.

You may have heard that "AI runs in the cloud," but it's not always clear what that changes for you. Two recent announcements make it easier to see. In both, an AI model does a real job: it looks at a picture or builds a video file, instead of only writing text back to you.

## Two different routes to the same idea

**The first route is a cloud platform.** A cloud platform is a company's computers, rented over the internet, that run an AI model for you. You never install anything. You send a request, and the model sends back an answer. Together AI describes one such option as "Serverless Inference," which means the provider handles the computers behind the scenes.

According to Together AI, Tencent's Hy4 is now available that way. Tencent calls Hy4 its flagship model, meaning its most capable one. Together says it is the first model in the Hy family that accepts images alongside text. A multimodal model (one that handles more than one kind of input, such as words and pictures) can look at a chart and describe it, for example.

Together also lists a 1-million-token context window. A token is a small chunk of text, and the context window is how much material the model can keep in view at once. In plain terms, it can work through a very long document or conversation in one go. That number comes from Together's announcement, so treat it as their claim.

**The second route is a connector.** A connector is a link that lets one app use another app's features. Picsart says its Media Studio is now live in Claude, Anthropic's AI assistant. You add it, sign in with your Picsart account, and then ask for what you want in ordinary words.

Claude can plan a video and write the script, but Picsart says the file itself is made by Media Studio. Picsart lists captions that highlight each word as it's spoken, transitions between clips, and resizing to the vertical 9:16 shape that phone screens prefer. Finished videos can be saved as MP4 or GIF files in your Picsart Drive, which is Picsart's cloud storage.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life**: If you've ever wished a family video had captions or a cleaner cut, the Picsart connector shows the idea. You describe the result, and the tool does the fiddly editing.
- **For your business or work**: Picsart names social media managers, small-business owners making promotions, and creators adding captions to talking-head clips as its intended users. Making a short vertical promo from your own footage, without opening a separate editor, is the kind of task it targets.
- **If you're just getting started**: Begin with something small. Ask Claude to plan a short video from clips you already have, and look at the preview before you approve the final render.
- **If you already use it**: Ask Media Studio for a contact sheet first. Picsart says it shows a strip of frames at set times in the chat, so you can check the cuts before the full video is rendered and saved to your Drive.

## What to keep in mind

Media Studio works with material you bring, plus Picsart's templates, effects and fonts. Picsart says it is not meant for making a video from a text prompt alone. Hy4 is aimed at developers who build with the model through Together's platform, so it is less of a button you press and more of a building block for software.

## Wrap-up

The main lesson is that AI is moving from "tell me something" toward "make this for me." A cloud model can read a picture, and a connector can turn your clips into a finished file. If you use Claude already, try the Picsart connector on one short clip this week, and see how much of the editing it handles for you.
